newsitem.title: USA: Esquire Communications posts loss, president resigns.
newsitem.headline: Esquire Communications posts loss, president resigns.

text.p: Esquire Communications Ltd. Wednesday reported a first-quarter loss and said David Feldman resigned as president and chief operating officer for personal reasons.

Feldman will remain a member of Esquire's board of directors and act as a consultant to the company, which is the nation's largest provider of court reporting and related legal support services, Esquire said.
As a result of Feldman's resignation, the New York-based company expects to record a pretax charge of about $1 million in the second quarter.

Esquire also said it lost $169,000, or 7 cents a share, before preferred dividends of $113,000, for the quarter ended March 31, due to five acquisitions completed between July and January. In the year-ago period, it earned $33,000 or 1 cent per share.
Revenues surged to $8.8 million from $5.5 million.
Esquire's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $3.50 on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.
